summary: Edith Tóth was an Indology, Tibetology, and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Lajos Ligeti, János Harmatta, and László Gaál (c. 1951–1956). She served as Keeper of the Indian collection at the Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts (c. 1956–1965).

Edith Wyschogrod was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. She earned her B.A. at Hunter College (c. 1947–1951) and her Ph.D. at Columbia University (c. 1964–1970), later serving as Professor of Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University (1992–2002).
Edmond Yee is a scholar in religious studies and Sinology. In 2003, he held faculty posts at both the Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union.
Edmund Charles Cox was a history and archaeology scholar. He was educated at Marlborough College from circa 1870 to 1874 and at Trinity College, Cambridge, from circa 1874 to 1877.

Edmund Hardy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earning a Ph.D. at Heidelberg and a Dr.theol. at Freiburg. He held posts at the University of Freiburg (1885–1893), University of Fribourg (1894–1898), and University of Würzburg (c. 1893–1904).

Edmund Henderson Hunt was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Harrow School and Balliol College, Oxford (c. 1893–1897). He served as Chief Medical Officer for the Nizam's Guaranteed State Railway from circa 1903 to 1931.

Edmund Husserl was a philosopher who studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Vienna, and Halle. He held academic positions at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (c. 1887–1901), the University of Göttingen (1901–1916), and the University of Freiburg (1916–1928).
Edmund Kleinhans was a linguist who studied at the University of Innsbruck under Friedrich Stolz and at the University of Leipzig under Karl Brugmann from 1892 to 1893.

Edmund Leach was an anthropologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Clare College and the LSE under Malinowski and Radcliffe-Brown. He taught at the LSE (c. 1947–1953) and Cambridge (1953–1978), where he also served as Provost of King's College.

Edmund Martin Küttler worked in Indology and linguistics, earning a Ph.D. at the University of Vienna. He taught at Masaryk University (1927) and served as Director of the Moravian Museum from circa 1939 to 1945.

Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard, Berlin, and Leipzig, where he earned his Ph.D. He taught Latin at Vassar College in 1890 and served as Professor of German and French at University School.
Edmund Stengel was a scholar who studied under Nikolaus Delius and Friedrich Christian Diez from circa 1864 to 1867.

Edmund W. Smith worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was appointed Assistant Archaeological Surveyor for the North-West Provinces and Oudh with the Archaeological Survey of India in 1886 and became Curator of the State Museum, Lucknow, in 1898.

Edo Shonin is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Nottingham Trent University. He is attested in 2015 as a research psychologist there and as Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre.

Edoardo Siani is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an M.A. at SOAS. He held researcher posts at SOAS (2018–2019) and Kyoto University (2018–2020), becoming an assistant professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 2020.

Edouard Müller-Hess was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig. He taught German at Cardiff University (1883–1888) and served as PD für Sanskrit (1881–1883) and Professor of Sanskrit (1888) at the University of Bern.

Eduard Buschmann was a linguist who studied under Franz Bopp in Berlin and at Göttingen. He served as Assistant at the Royal Library of Berlin (1832) and held posts at the Prussian Academy of Sciences and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Eduard Böhmer was a linguist who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1847 to 1851. He held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1859–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (c. 1872–1879).

Eduard Erkes was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Leipzig under August Conrady. He later held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (c. 1917–1958) and Humboldt University of Berlin (c. 1952–1958).

Eduard Hermann was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Jena under Berthold Delbrück. He held professorships at Kiel University (1913), Goethe University Frankfurt (1914), and the University of Göttingen (1917–1937).
